BiblicalUsage: This Aramaic word means to come or to arrive, and it carries the turning points of Daniel. Nebuchadnezzar came near the furnace and called the three men out, the vessels of God's house were brought into Belshazzar's feast, and Daniel saw one like the Son of man come with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word keeps pointing forward, because the coming that matters most is the Son of man coming to receive His kingdom. The furnace and the feast both ended in judgment, and I hold that His coming will end in a kingdom that never passes away.
